learning_outcomes.text: Using measurement techniques for electrical and non-electrical quantities and data acquisition systems in electromechanical systems
Operating, maintenance, service, system integration activities
Students acquire the concepts regarding technological methods and procedures, methods of analysis and synthesis of their structure.
Applying general and specialized technical knowledge to solve the logistic problems specific to the field of electrical engineering.
Design and use of schemes, structural and functional diagrams, graphic representations and technical documents specific to the field of electrical engineering.

syllabus_topics: Basic concepts of technological methods and processes
Elements of technical norming in the technological process
Precision of part and product processing. Tolerances and adjustments
Metals and alloys used in electrical engineering
Electrical insulating materials used in electrical engineering
Methods and processes of cold machining
Methods and processes for splitting machining
Methods and processes for processing materials by cutting and cold plastic deformation
Method of heating ingots using superconducting magnets
Pipe welding technology in a hyperbaric environment
Technology of material processing by solidification with phase change surface control
Corrosion and corrosion protection of metals and alloys
Corrosion protection of metals and alloys
Presentation of the paper, instructions on the work safety rules, processing of the experimental data
Standardization in the machine industry and in electrical engineering
Metals and alloys used in the electrotechnical industry
teaching_methods: Course (Projector, intercalated student contributions and debates)
Laboratory (Presentation of the paper, test on theoretical knowledge, interpretation of results)
assessment_rules: The final grade (VP Grade) is calculated as 0.5 * VPF + 0.5 * LF. LF = 0.45 * OL + 0.05 * R. VPF = (VPI + VPII) / 2. A minimum mark of 5 is required for both the course and laboratory components. Attendance at laboratory classes below 70% leads to the restoration of the discipline. Recovery of one missed laboratory is allowed. The minimum performance standard involves carrying out works under coordination with correct evaluation of workload, resources, time, risks, and safety norms, and adequate use of basic knowledge of technological methods and processes.
